steps.name: Red
steps.text: Right, now I remember. That's the Rhodes Island uniform.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Mr. Guard has a set of it, and if memory serves, Miss Susie went to some Rhodes Island after leaving Caladon too.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: They should be a good bunch. Why help Miss Susie otherwise?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: And they're helping the Infected here too.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: *sigh* It's tough being the good ones. The good ones always choose too much responsibility for themselves.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: All while some responsibilities weren't meant for anyone to bear.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Poor Rhodes Island. Maybe they went down the wrong path from square one.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Just like Nine said, injections and tablets won't solve Oripathy. The body can hurt less, but others won't change the way they look at you so easily.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: We need to force them to see us, to hear our voices, to admit we're not just sores and ulcers on them.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: You've been with me long enough, friends. Any brilliant ideas about what I just mentioned?
Reunion.
You aren't part of our objective.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: So I'm guessing we can keep doing each to our own?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Fine, leave then.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Well, since Dublinn is in the mix now, it's about time I get them evacuated.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Grr. If I had a little more time, I could've talked a few more people over.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: For now, let's go rendezvous with her.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You call yourself a poet...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Miss Ines. Another marvelous insight to share?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I've met a few poets before, all far better than you, because—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: They never misused their metaphors.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Dust, sandpaper...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Out of this plate, this nation, even the entire land itself, who's the dust, and who's the sandpaper?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And how are you qualified to decide who's who?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: War doesn't do metaphor in any way.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's not some terrific journey. It's not some furnace for glory once again. It's not some ship sailing for revival.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's just people struggling in mud. Arms broken in ruins. Stenches that never fade.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's all it is.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...I know that better than anyone.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: We can set aside our differences for now. I respect the views of a veteran mercenary.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But I do need an answer as to my proposal for promoting from pawn to friend.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She's agreed, as long as both we and her can leave this place alive.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She's already left for the comms station. The broadcast will be out imminently.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: There's a shame. We didn't need to go that far.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You've turned down an invitation from Victoria.

options: The Duke of Caster can't stand for all of Victoria.
All I've turned down is a lousy poet.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She will.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Not a wise decision, I have to say.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Being clever won't help you, Doctor of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Is this one of your little schemes too?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Delphine? What are you...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Run! They're—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You...

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: What a clamorous locale.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Should I refer to you as Captain of the Redsteel Guard, or 'The Brigadier' of Dublinn?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Such a surprise to see your people here.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Finally, an end to the slog.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Delphine and that Doctor will sort out that comms station, right?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: It'll all go smooth, and then we can leave Norport.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Figured out where you're off to after?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: ...Dunno.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Anyone mucking in a Norport gang either came out an orphanage or plain lost anyone to fall back on.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Goes for us too pretty much, I figure.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: There'll be a way. We'll find some way to feed ourselves. Hah, maybe I'll go off and join those 'Rusthammers.' They love to tell stories about them, don't they.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Won't catch me dead being a duke's estate refugee at any rate, down on my knees begging those ivory tower shits for my bowl of gruel.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Cador—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I know. You think I'm still on about some naive shit, like 'ooh, let's knock the daylights out of the Sarkaz' was.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Baird, I've lost enough living through all this. I can't just abandon the final specks I still have.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: All this... pain, this torment, if it turns me, crushes me soft after all, then I may as well be dead in an alley.

spans.text: All this... pain, this torment, if it turns me, crushes me soft after all, then I may as well

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: It's... maybe hard to criticize being crushed, Cador. Nobody's actually got a spine of steel.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: During the day, I went to the video shop. McClaren wasn't there fighting over that luggage thing of supplies, so I thought he might've had an accident.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: He always thinks everyone's up to something, the weirdo.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You've gone and drunk plenty of his squash, haven't you.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Fine, then, may he live forevermore. He alright?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: ...He still alive?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Front of the video shop was wretched. I'd guess he's been raided a bunch.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I tried calling for him, but no response. So I thought he was hiding somewhere else, until... I saw him. Through his window all nailed shut, just a crack left. Saw his eyes.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Bulging out of their sockets. Covered in blood. Terrified. Desperate. Didn't dare look at him again.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: He—

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I don't think he can come out of there anymore.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You say 'soft.' You call them that. But we know we're... not that far off ourselves.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We still have a chance to save all this.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It'll be tough. We'll have to survive the Sarkaz's likely counterattack, and then the artillery from the dukes' forces.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But it's not at all impossible.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Right now, we need to figure out what moves the Sarkaz barracks are going to make against us...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hrmph. Always on time to encourage us and remind us what we need to do, Your Majesty. How reliable of you.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Cador...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Oh, might I have the privilege of your orders again?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm wondering... what would you say—a king is?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: What, you taking me in as your vassal?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, I've said it a thousand times, I'm just Vina of the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I just... realized I never honestly thought about the question before.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Maybe I'm clueless how, aside from all that praise about honor and majesty, what a king is to you...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, to us, as a thing that exists.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: It doesn't. It's nothing.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: No king's ever meant shit to us. I'm happier giving my respect to the tuck shop owner who does a discount for me when I've not got enough in my purse.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Victoria's always had a king, since ancient times.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Yeah? And who were they? Because I'm terribly sorry, but I'm not some hoity-toity Aslan or Draco, and I've never met one neither.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: If they're nowhere except a few names in a book, then I know Chef Vito off the Siracusan restaurant ads better than I do them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: We haven't had a king for how many years. Are our lives any worse?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Fine, maybe they are.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But I really doubt it's anything to do with whether we've got a king or not. Don't care if it's you or whatever heavyweight taking the throne, you're not gonna be looking us down here in the eye.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: By your definitions, a foolish king gets lost in banquets and wine, while a wise king draws up war and taxes.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: If you ask me, it's ego-chasing no matter which. The vanity of thinking you can control everything, full stop.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Siege, everyone in Norport's bowing down to you as their one hope...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: So you tell me. You having fun?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You think saving them is your glorious bloody calling?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'd never say 'calling.' Never.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Just—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Just, you think you've got some kind of responsibility. Like they're watching you and you need to answer them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Some bloody mess you're in. Poor old Royal Highness.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I'd ask, but you know full well. Are they willing to pin their sights on you because you're a member of a street gang—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: —or because of your bombshell of a surname, 'Victoria?'

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I'll be frank, I've just as much been hoping for someone to save all this, save all of us, save this bloody endless cesspit.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And who's going to do that? Quit dreaming.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Daring to bear the responsibility's a fine moral thing that helps us muck our way in the streets, Siege.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But don't give people false hope with that 'king' persona.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And don't... ever buy—that they were right to expect this shit of you since the day you were born.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Got visitors.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Tch. Do we do them in?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Don't jump to anything. We don't want to tip them off. We just need a grasp of how they're deployed for now...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Something's off. Be on high alert.

steps.name: Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: You... lot...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Don't get the wrong idea, sir, we're not here for trouble, just passing by...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Baird! Didn't you say don't tip them off?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Shit—I didn't do anything!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This blood... He was already badly injured. He was fleeing this way.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Someone in the lockdown take him to task?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Don't think so. Not like we haven't tried before. Maybe there's a chance to take one or two out, but it's a whole army keeping us in here.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Even if a sneak attack goes well, they'll retaliate fast. Unless...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Is it... usually this quiet around here?
From atop the zone's walls, searchlights throw down beams of death-pale white.
They're well-versed in the odors that pervade Norport, but here, the smell of fresh blood fills the air.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Get out of here, fast.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We need to gather every citizen we can still find on this plate.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But we still don't have word back from Miss Ines and the Doctor.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We'll just have to assume for now their side's going smooth.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Someone's already made a move here.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: You're sure?

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: I'm sure. That's an Aslan.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: She's not part of our objective.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: That's fine. She'll make the call herself.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Dammit, the door here's been sealed.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Doctor, stay behind me.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Everyone, a warm welcome to the Sunset Street Hotel. We haven't had this many esteemed visitors in a very long time.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Colbert! I told you to stay hidden!

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Not receiving guests at the door would be my failure as the owner of a hotel.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I'm very sorry for how limited we are under present conditions. I'd have some complimentary tea brought out to you all, otherwise.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Is there anything I might be able to help you with?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Do you have normal water, then? I am, er... a bit thirsty, actually.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: That, I can serve you, Miss Delphine.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Old Wellington wasn't willing to let this place off after all.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Nor Duke Caster.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Would you allow me to leave now?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: You and that blue-haired Feline are staying.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I imagine the Duke of Caster and the Duke of Wellington have an unspoken agreement on the 'standing off against the Sarkaz' front.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And as for the goals of each one of us... some unspoken agreement too.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I simply obey the orders I receive.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Are all Tarans as dreary as you?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: My sense of humor is reserved for my friends.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Wonderful, I love making friends. Being fellow Victorians, why don't we start by complaining about the weather?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Yes, the weather... Londinium's has been horrible, and it's only getting worse.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: We actually saw the sun some days, forty years ago.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Our hotel was much better then than now, too. What an incredible place it was!

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I still remember to this day when I first came on as the doorman.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I hear back then, even the dukes loved staying here!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Your presence isn't needed, Sarkaz.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Sir, I'm truly sorry, but it's my hope you'll regard me as a Victorian much like you.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: We are all the people of Victoria. What need do we have for tensions like this, no?

spans.text: all the people of Victoria. What need do we have for tensions like this, no?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Rare to see a Sarkaz self-identifying as a Victorian.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Isn't your case much along the same lines as mine, Miss?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Us Sarkaz living outside of Kazdel have to find a home for ourselves, don't we?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I'm afraid most Sarkaz don't think so.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Hence why they're always so despondent, so weary.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: In my view, well, I've lived here all my life, and every wall and every floor is a familiar one to me, far more familiar than Kazdel so far away.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Pardon my negligence these days, but I'd wipe every table spotless by myself in older times.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I was proud of my work. You really should've seen what it was like back then.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Oh, different times... they put me under the illusion that days like those would last forever.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: *sigh* But times like those come to an end.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Percival, it really is a shame you came to work here after the place declined.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: To be honest, I don't really care that much.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: If it was as ravaged by war and shaken to rubble as everything else now, honestly, I might be taking things better myself.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: What hurts me is...

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: On an afternoon like all the afternoons that used to be, I finished wiping the tables, lifted my head—

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: And it suddenly hit me, how old everything around me was.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: And I was clueless how it even happened.
